review_notes: No change requested. Correctness: `hasProd_one_add_of_hasSum_prod` unfolds `HasProd` to the limit of the finite products ∏ i ∈ s, (1 + f i). `Finset.prod_one_add` (from the new import, which is therefore used) rewrites each of these as ∑ t ∈ s.powerset, ∏ i ∈ t, f i. Composing `h` with the fact that `powerset` tends to atTop then gives exactly the goal. Each lemma uses only the assumptions it needs: CommSemiring and TopologicalSpace, with T2Space only for `tprod_eq`. The one-way statement is right; the converse fails, e.g. with f i = -1. Alternatives I considered and did not file: (1) Renaming `tprod_one_add` to `Summable.tprod_one_add`. The 2025-04-12 deprecations in this file move summability-conditional tsum lemmas into the `Summable` namespace, but those renames free up root names for unconditional versions. Here no unconditional version is possible, because the identity is false without summability. So this is a naming preference, not a defect. (2) Shortening the `multipliable_one_add_of_summable_prod` proof to `(hasProd_one_add_of_hasSum_prod h.hasSum).multipliable`: a style preference. (3) Adding docstrings to `hasProd_one_add_of_hasSum_prod` and `tprod_one_add`, and adding the missing article in 'For complete normed ring': cosmetic. (4) The docstring refers to `multipliable_one_add_of_summable`, which this diff does not add. The packet cannot confirm or rule out that the lemma exists elsewhere in Mathlib (e.g. Analysis/Normed/Ring/InfiniteSum). A docstring reference is not checked by the compiler, so I did not report it as a defect.
